name: Question 7
problem: Using the standard form of the Maclaurin series of $\frac{1}{1-x},$ find the first three non-zero terms of the series expansion of the definite integral ${\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{4}{4-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.$
worked_solution:
Note that

$$
\frac{4}{4-{x}^{2}}=\frac{1}{(1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4})}.
$$

The power series expansion of $\frac{1}{1-x}$ is given by 

$$
\frac{1}{1-x}=1+x+{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

Replacing $x$ with $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}$ in the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{(1-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4})} & =1+\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{4}{4-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(1+\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{x}^{4}}{16}+⋯)\text{d}x \\  & =(x+\frac{{x}^{3}}{12}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{80}+⋯){|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =1+\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{80}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

Using the standard form of the Maclaurin series of 11−x, find the first three non-zero terms of the series expansion of the definite integral ∫0144−x2dx.

a
 ∫0144−x2dx=1+112+180+⋯
b
 ∫0144−x2dx=4+14+116+⋯
c
 ∫0144−x2dx=4+112+140+⋯
d
 ∫0144−x2dx=1+14+18+⋯
e
 ∫0144−x2dx=1+13+120+⋯
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Note that 44−x2=1(1−x24).

The power series expansion of 11−x is given by 11−x=1+x+x2+⋯.

Replacing x with x24 in the above, we get

1(1−x24)=1+x24+x416+⋯.

Finally, we calculate the definite integral:

∫0144−x2dx=∫01(1+x24+x416+⋯)dx=(x+x312+x580+⋯)|01=1+112+180+⋯
